contradictions: MEDIA ARCHITECTURE. webview-media recommends capture plus WebCodecs encode in the webview, shipping getDisplayMedia first. media-pipeline recommends native Rust (cpal, sonora, Opus, WGC, Media Foundation H.264) with the webview only decoding. One of media-pipeline's three reasons for rejecting option B is refuted by webview-media's measurement: wry 0.57.3 never calls SetIsVisible(false). Over 6 minutes minimized or hidden, timers, rAF, Channel delivery and AudioWorklet were not throttled. The two reasons that still stand are WebView2 AEC for webview-played audio (medium confidence in both reports, untested) and WebView2Feedback #5763 (still open; I checked). Resolution: native audio and capture still wins, but on those grounds, not on throttling.

DEAD TRIGGER. media-pipeline's viewer spec says to unsubscribe video on visibilitychange to hidden. On this stack that event never fires on minimize or hide, because webview-media measured visibilityState staying 'visible'. The 'pause rAF when minimized' advice has the same problem. Drive both from native Tauri window events (minimized, hidden, focus), not from Page Visibility.

CONNECTION/ALPN LAYOUT. The reports give three incompatible layouts:
- iroh: one ALPN, tincan/control/1, for chat, election and media; large video frames on short-lived per-frame uni streams.
- media-pipeline: a separate tincan/media/1 connection with its own QuicTransportConfig (BBR3, small datagram send buffer); one uni stream per GOP.
- protocol: tincan/server/1 plus tincan/dm/1, with 1:1 calls on the DM connection.
Transport config is fixed when a connection is dialled or accepted (ConnectOptions::with_transport_config / Incoming::accept_with). So 'calls on the DM connection' conflicts with media-pipeline's media-tuned config unless DM connections are always dialled with it.

ATTACHMENT HOLDERS vs NON-AUTHORITATIVE HOST. The iroh report has the host keep a per-hash holders list and inject it into each attachment message. The protocol report makes every event author-signed: its Attachment struct is {blob, size, name, mime} with no holders field, and the host holds no unique state. Neither report says where 'who holds hash X' lives, or how it survives host migration. The user's 'download keeps going when the uploader is offline' requirement depends on exactly that.

HOST ELIGIBILITY.
- media-pipeline: a relay-only member is never host, and election must weigh measured uplink (host upload is about 11-13 Mbps for one 1080p share to 5 viewers).
- protocol: tier 0 (relay only) stays eligible, with a lowest-UserId fallback, and the score has no uplink term at all.

UNSTABLE API IN ELECTION. The protocol report's tier score depends on Endpoint::net_report(), which is gated behind iroh's 'unstable-net-report' feature (confirmed cfg-gated in iroh 1.5.0 endpoint.rs). The iroh report scores stability from the stable conn.paths() data and advises hiding churning APIs behind internal traits.

FIREWALL vs INSTALL MODE. The iroh report says the installer should add a Windows Firewall rule. webview-media recommends NSIS installMode 'currentUser', which has no admin prompt. Adding firewall rules needs elevation, so both cannot hold. The choice is perMachine (one UAC prompt) or accepting the first-run firewall prompt. The elevation requirement is standard Windows behaviour; I did not re-verify it this session.

RELAY TIMING. The iroh report says to run your own iroh-relay (or pay for n0 Pro) before any public release. The protocol report defers a self-hosted relay and DNS to later. media-pipeline says 'eventually'. This is the one piece of infrastructure that breaks 'nobody runs a server', and the three reports disagree on when it is needed.

DHT STACKS. The iroh report calls the Mainline DHT address lookup 'one line to add later'. The protocol report uses n0-mainline 0.8.0 directly for rendezvous records. The latest iroh-mainline-address-lookup (0.6.1, 2026-10-20) still requires n0-mainline ^0.7, so using both puts two DHT implementations in one binary.

VIDEO FRAMING. The iroh report puts each large video frame on its own short-lived uni stream. media-pipeline uses one uni stream per GOP, with set_priority(group_seq) and reset-on-drop. These are different drop and priority semantics.

DATAGRAM BUFFERS. media-pipeline recommends datagram_receive_buffer_size 64 KiB, but its own snippet uses 256 KiB, and the iroh spike sets 1 MiB. The setting that matters for latency is a small datagram_send_buffer_size. noq drops the oldest datagrams only when that buffer is full, and the default is 1 MiB.

ECHO CANCELLATION.
- webview-media: rely on Chrome-wide AEC to cancel AudioWorklet playback.
- media-pipeline: cites a Zoom forum report of echo in Edge, saying Edge only cancels audio Edge itself plays.
Both are medium confidence and cannot be resolved without a two-machine test. The question is moot if all call audio is native.

WEBCODECS RESULTS ON THE SAME MACHINE.
- AV1 and VP9 hardware encode disagreement: resolved (see corrections).
- HEVC decoder: webview-media says hardware only; media-pipeline says hardware and software, but its probe only tested prefer-hardware.
- H.264 hardware encode tail latency is unresolved: p99 355 ms (webview-media) vs p95 about 46 ms (media-pipeline). Both are single runs reporting different percentiles.

VERSION PINNING. The protocol report pins iroh '=1.5.0'; the iroh report uses '1.5'. n0 says only the latest stable iroh is officially supported on its public relays, so an exact pin goes stale within weeks. Either way, an auto-update path is required, and no report designed one.

API NAME. The protocol report calls the per-path type 'PathInfo'. In iroh 1.5.0 it is iroh::endpoint::Path (re-exported from socket/remote_map/remote_state/path_watcher.rs), returned by Connection::paths() -> PathList.

verified_corrections.claim: iroh report: the blobs protocol has no 'which ranges do you have' query, so a partial holder can only be discovered by trying to download from it.
verified_corrections.finding:
Wrong. Verified by compiling and running. iroh-blobs 0.105.0 has a Request::Observe wire request. The client calls store.remote().observe(conn, ObserveRequest::new(hash)) and gets a stream: first the provider's Bitfield {size, ChunkRanges}, then live diffs as the provider acquires more data.

In a 3-node run in my scratch project:
- B had fetched only bytes 0..256 KiB from A.
- C observing B got size=1048576, ranges=RangeSet{0..256}, complete=false.
- C observing A got RangeSet{0..}, complete=true.

Observe is off by default. EventMask::DEFAULT has observe: ObserveMode::Disabled, and a provider with the default mask reset the stream (ConnectionReset, Reset(1)) even though it held the full blob. To enable it, use BlobsProtocol::new(&store, Some(tx)) with (tx, rx) = EventSender::channel(32, EventMask { observe: ObserveMode::None /* or Notify, or Intercept for a member check */, ..EventMask::DEFAULT }).

The module doc comment in protocol.rs ('does not yet have a discovery mechanism') is stale. Content discovery (which peers have a hash) still does not exist; Observe only answers for a peer you already know.

verified_corrections.claim: media-pipeline: rate-limit iroh-blobs to about 50% of uplink during calls, using a home-made token bucket (no built-in hook was identified).
verified_corrections.finding: There is a built-in hook. Confidence: high, from reading the source; not run. EventMask.throttle = ThrottleMode::Intercept makes the provider raise a ProviderMessage::Throttle {connection_id, request_id, size} for each chunk sent, which the source says will usually be 16 KiB. Delaying the reply should therefore pace uploads; this is inferred from the code path, not measured. AbortReason::RateLimited also exists for rejecting a request outright.

verified_corrections.claim: media-pipeline open question: how do noq DATAGRAM frames get scheduled relative to STREAM frames, and does audio stay low-latency while a video stream is backlogged?
verified_corrections.finding:
Partly answered. Confidence: verified from source, not measured under congestion. In noq-proto 1.5.0, Connection::populate_packet writes queued DATAGRAM frames in a loop, until datagrams or frame space run out, before it calls streams.write_stream_frames.

So inside one connection, audio datagrams go out ahead of any queued video stream bytes in every packet. Both are still gated per packet by the same congestion window (in_flight + bytes_to_send > congestion.window() leads to PathBlocked::Congestion) and by pacing.

Outgoing drop-oldest happens only when datagram_send_buffer_size is exceeded (default 1 MiB). The receive side drops the oldest datagrams when its window is exceeded.

Implication: put audio and video on the same connection so they share one congestion controller. Separate media connections would compete with each other on the host's uplink.

verified_corrections.claim: Reports assume there is no built-in way to get an uplink or throughput signal for host election.
verified_corrections.finding:
Confidence: verified from source. iroh 1.5.0 Path::stats() returns noq PathStats, which has `bandwidth_estimate: Option<u64>` (bits/s) next to `cwnd`, `rtt` and `congestion_events`.

Only BBR3 fills it in: bbr3/mod.rs returns max_bw*8. CubicConfig, which is the noq default, and NewReno return None. So the signal exists only if the connection uses Bbr3Config, which media-pipeline only compile-checked.

It is a per-path, per-peer delivery-rate estimate. I expect it to reflect traffic actually sent, not spare uplink capacity; that is inference, not verified. So it does not by itself solve 'measure a candidate's uplink before electing it'.

verified_corrections.claim: iroh report: FsStore always spawns one thread per core; the only knob is the process-wide TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS, which 'also caps Tauri's tokio runtime'.
verified_corrections.finding:
Half right. Confidence: verified from source.
- FsStore::load_with_opts builds tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread() with only thread_name_fn and enable_time. fs::Options has fields {path, inline, batch, gc, crash_consistency} and no runtime or worker setting, so the env var is indeed the only knob for FsStore.
- But the env var does not have to cap Tauri. tauri 2.12.7 exposes tauri::async_runtime::set(handle: TokioHandle), so the app can build its own runtime with an explicit .worker_threads(n). tokio 1.54.1 docs say an explicit worker_threads overrides TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS.
- Pattern: own runtime for Tauri plus iroh with a fixed size; env var set before FsStore::load only to bound the store runtime.

unanswered: HOLDER INDEX (user requirement). No report says where 'who holds hash X' lives, or how it is rebuilt after host migration or a partition. A candidate design: online members announce held hashes as ephemeral presence; the current host aggregates them into the roster; a downloader Observes candidate peers (now verified possible) before fetching. It is undesigned and untested.

UPLOADER LEAVES FIRST. If the uploader goes offline before anyone has fetched the data, nobody can serve it. Should the host, or N members, auto-prefetch attachments, and up to what size and disk cap? This determines whether 'download keeps going if the host is offline' actually holds.

UPLINK MEASUREMENT FOR HOST ELECTION. BBR3's per-path bandwidth_estimate exists, but it only reflects traffic actually sent, and Cubic is the default. Nobody specified an active probe, or how a candidate's upload capacity is learned before it is asked to forward 11-13 Mbps.

WAN BEHAVIOUR. Every number in every report came from one machine. Still unmeasured: hole-punch success between two residential NATs; the share of pairs that stay relayed; throughput and latency on relay paths; max_datagram_size on a relay path. The test is two Windows machines on different ISPs, including one behind CGNAT or a phone hotspot.

PUBLIC RELAY LIMITS. The numbers are unpublished; the docs only say limiting is per-connection token-bucket backpressure. Unknown whether a relayed 1-2.5 Mbps screen share or 60 kbps audio survives it. Unknown whether per-connection limiting means a host with N relayed members gets N buckets, or whether per-IP limits also apply.

AEC QUALITY. sonora 0.3 has not been tested in a real room (laptop speakers, double-talk, USB/HDMI clock drift). The C++ fallback, webrtc-audio-processing bundled, needs meson, ninja, pkg-config and clang, which are not on the machine. Needs a two-machine recorded test.

FIREWALL AND INSTALL. Do direct paths and mDNS still work when a per-user install has no firewall rule, or the user dismisses the first-run prompt, which can create inbound Block rules? Only a two-machine test can answer it, and the answer decides between perMachine and currentUser install.

IN-CALL RESOURCES. WebView2 is about 154 MB private at idle, against roughly 10 MB for the iroh core. Nobody measured RAM and CPU with a real React UI decoding 1-4 video streams during a call, nor the cost of a host forwarding to 5-25 members. A non-webview UI was not considered against the 'minimum resources' requirement.

SYSTEM AUDIO IN SCREEN SHARE. The user did not request it; Discord offers it. WASAPI process loopback needs Windows build 20348 or later according to Microsoft's docs, which leaves out Windows 10 22H2 clients (19045). wasapi 0.27.0 exposes AudioClient::new_application_loopback_client(process_id: u32, include_tree: bool). Whether it can express PROCESS_LOOPBACK_MODE_EXCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE, which is needed to keep call audio out of the share, is unconfirmed.
WGC CAPTURE BORDER. Not checked: the yellow capture border, and borderless capture access (GraphicsCaptureAccess with Borderless) for an unpackaged Win32 Tauri app.

SCHEDULING UNDER CONGESTION. The source shows datagrams go out ahead of stream data, but behaviour on a shaped link (audio latency while a video GOP backlog fills cwnd, and BBR3 vs Cubic) is unmeasured. BBR3 was only ever compile-checked.

CODEC CRATES.
- unsafe-libopus has not been published since 2024-11-21. A maintained replacement (C libopus via the opus/audiopus crates with a bundled build) was not build-tested on MSVC.
- moq-video's license and the effort to vendor only its WGC and MF backend were not checked.
#5763 ON RUNTIME 157. Untested whether the getDisplayMedia deadlock reproduces on WebView2 157. It only matters if getDisplayMedia is kept as a fallback.

PRODUCT SCOPE. Open: should the voice SFU host always be the text host, or should voice rooms elect their own media host? Also undecided: target server size, history and blob retention caps, and multi-device support. All are flagged by the protocol report and still unresolved.
overall_recommendation:
Keep media-pipeline's native direction, but for the right reasons. Audio should be native Rust: cpal, sonora AEC3, and Opus (track unsafe-libopus's staleness). Screen capture should be native WGC plus Media Foundation hardware H.264. The webview should only decode, using WebCodecs VideoDecoder fed by a raw Tauri Channel. The reasons that hold are an exact AEC reference, which native playback gives, and the still-open #5763 deadlock. Background throttling is not a reason: it was measured as absent on wry 0.57.3. Drive any 'pause video or rAF when minimized' logic from Tauri window events, because visibilitychange never fires.

Connection layout: use one iroh connection per member-to-host link on one ALPN (for example tincan/server/1). It carries:
- the control and sync bi stream;
- Opus as datagrams;
- video as one uni stream per GOP with set_priority.
Dial it with a media-tuned QuicTransportConfig: small datagram_send_buffer_size, max_idle_timeout about 10 s, keep-alive about 2 s, and BBR3 A/B-tested against Cubic. noq writes datagrams ahead of stream data inside a connection, and a single congestion controller avoids self-competition. Dial tincan/dm/1 with the same config so 1:1 calls can run on it. Blobs go peer-to-peer on iroh_blobs::ALPN with:
- ObserveMode::Intercept, used both to check membership and to query a candidate's ranges;
- ThrottleMode::Intercept, to cap seeding during calls;
- a pool connect_timeout of 3-5 s.

Close the holder-index gap explicitly: an ephemeral 'I hold X' presence aggregated by whichever member is host, plus an auto-prefetch policy. Without it the offline-download requirement is not met.

Host election:
- Exclude relay-only candidates whenever a direct candidate exists.
- Add an uplink term, either from BBR3 bandwidth_estimate on live host connections or from an active probe.
- Keep the unstable-net-report dependency behind an internal trait.

Infrastructure: treat relays as the one server Tincan needs. n0's public relays are dev/hobby per the relays docs; the DNS page's 'production welcome' line conflicts and should not be relied on. Budget a self-hosted iroh-relay or n0 Pro ($19/mo) before any public release. Pair that with an auto-updater and code signing, since n0 supports only the latest iroh.

Decide the install mode now: perMachine plus a firewall rule, or currentUser plus accepting the prompt.

Dependencies: the combined stack type-checks with a single windows, tokio, iroh and noq. Pin iroh-blobs =0.105.0 behind a trait. Vendor moq-video's WGC and MF backend rather than taking its 42 extra crates.
